A knight's move always changes the color of its square. The knight starts on a1, a dark square, so after an odd number of moves (2009) it must be on a light square. There are 32 light squares.

Every light square is reachable. The knight's graph on the board is connected, and any square is within a small number of moves of a1 (at most 6). Whenever a square is reachable in k moves, it is also reachable in k + 2 moves by moving to a neighbor and back. Since the parity of the move count matches for every light square, each one can be reached in exactly 2009 moves.

ANSWER: 32
